[Paris-Saclay University](/universities/12465/paris-saclay-university.html) Main campus: [Paris](/cities/55/paris.html), [France](/countries/10/france.html) [Top 0.7% worldwide Studyportals University Meta Ranking](/search/universities/master/rankings) 4.1 Read 29 reviews ## Key information ### Duration * Full-time + 12 months ### Start dates & application deadlines * Starting + Apply before ### Language English ### Credits 60 ECTS ### Delivered On Campus ### Campus Location * Paris, France ### Disciplines [Computer Sciences](/disciplines/281/computer-sciences.html "Computer Sciences") [Data Science & Big Data](/disciplines/282/data-science-big-data.html "Data Science & Big Data") [Software Engineering](/disciplines/329/software-engineering.html "Software Engineering") [View 58 other Masters in Data Science & Big Data in France](/study-options/268599578/data-science-big-data-france.html "View 58 other Masters in Data Science & Big Data in France") ## Overview The M1 Parisian Research Master in Computer Science (MPRI) at Paris-Saclay University is a comprehensive programme aimed at equipping students with the necessary skills for a successful research career or further doctoral studies in computer science. This master's programme is distinguished by its two primary tracks: the ENS Paris-Saclay track and the Faculty of Science track, both leading to the same M2 MPRI degree. Each track has its unique focus—while the ENS track emphasises the perfection of fundamental skills and their applications in computer science theory, the Faculty of Science track is dedicated to building robust foundations in theoretical computer science. Both tracks culminate in an extensive research internship, allowing students to apply their knowledge in a practical setting. The curriculum covers a wide array of topics, including but not limited to algorithmics, computability and complexity, automata theory, combinatorial and effective algebra, and programming language semantics. Additionally, students will delve into advanced fields such as cryptology, security, and quantum computing, depending on their chosen track. The programme is taught by leading researchers and practitioners in the field, ensuring that students receive cutting-edge knowledge and insights into current scientific advancements. All courses are primarily conducted in English, with a few exceptions at the Faculty of Science track, where students can opt for French-taught classes. The programme also offers a limited number of scholarships to assist with living costs, with application deadlines typically in May. **Why M1 Parisian Research Master in Computer Science at Paris-Saclay University?** Paris-Saclay University is renowned for its high academic standards and strong emphasis on research and innovation. The university's partnerships with various research institutions and industries enhance the learning experience, providing students with ample opportunities for collaboration and networking. The cutting-edge facilities and resources available to students further support their academic journey, making this programme an excellent choice for aspiring computer scientists. **Tuition Fee Breakdown** The tuition fees for the M1 Parisian Research Master in Computer Science are set at EUR 250 per year for both international and European students. For detailed information regarding the breakdown of fees in your local currency, please visit the Fees and Funding section. **Syllabus** * Algorithms in the Nature * Advanced Algorithms * Graph Algorithms * Parallel Algorithms * Probabilistic Algorithms and Games * Foundations of Quantum Information * Introduction to Quantum Algorithms and Programming * Foundations of Computer Science * General Computer Science * Initiation to Research * Elective Courses In addition to the core modules, students may select from a variety of elective courses that align with their interests and career aspirations, allowing for a tailored educational experience. The programme is structured to provide a balance of theoretical knowledge and practical application, preparing graduates for diverse roles in academia, research, and industry. **Careers with M1 Parisian Research Master in Computer Science** Graduates of the M1 Parisian Research Master in Computer Science often pursue further studies in the M2 MPRI programme or other specialised master's degrees. Career prospects include academic research positions, teaching roles at higher education institutions, and research and development roles in various sectors, such as technology, finance, and healthcare. Alumni have successfully transitioned into influential positions within leading tech companies and research organisations. ## Programme Structure **Courses include:** * Fundamental Informatics * Programming Languages * Machine Learning * Interactive Information Visualization * Algorithms for Data Science * Internet of Things * Fundamentals of Human-Computer Interaction Check your academic match with this programme ## Academic requirements We are not aware of any specific GRE, GMAT or GPA grading score requirements for this programme. ## English requirements We are not aware of any English requirements for this programme. ## Other requirements ### General requirements * Selection sheet for continuation in M2 to download on this web page. * Motivation letter. * All transcripts of the years / semesters validated since the high school diploma at the date of application. * Curriculum Vitae. * VAP file (obligatory for all persons requesting a valuation of the assets to enter the diploma). ## Student Insurance via Studyportals Partner Make sure to cover your health, travel, and stay while studying abroad. It offers an excellent preparation to [M2 MPRI](https://mpri-master.ens.fr/). The year’s objective is to perfect fundamental skills and discover their various applications in Computer Science theory. It culminates in a long research internship. The main fields covered are: algorithmics; computability and complexity; automata theory; combinatorial and effective algebra; logic, interactive and automatic demonstration; semantics of programming languages; analysis and verification of systems and programmes; cryptology and security.
